title: Vikings plan to pick up wide receiver Jordan Addison’s fifth-year option: Sources
content:
PHOENIX — The Minnesota Vikings plan to pick up wide receiver Jordan Addison’s fifth-year option, according to multiple team sources.

Addison, 24, is emerging from a down season. He caught 42 passes for 610 yards and three touchdowns. The Vikings expect the former first-round pick to produce more as part of an entire offensive uptick in 2026. For receivers with Addison’s play time, the projected contract value is $18 million, according to Over The Cap. That would put Addison around the 20th-highest-paid receiver in the league.

Minnesota faced a May 1 deadline on this decision. The Vikings still view Addison as a key cog of their passing attack. He was initially drafted in 2023 to alleviate the coverage burden on superstar receiver Justin Jefferson. Addison caught a combined 133 passes for more than 1,700 yards in his first two seasons.

As far as a long-term extension is concerned, the Vikings will monitor Addison’s consistency and production throughout the summer and into the fall. Addison was suspended at the start of the 2025 season for violating the NFL’s substance abuse policy. He was also benched in Week 5 in London because of a head-coaching decision.

Earlier this winter, Addison was arrested on a misdemeanor trespassing charge at the Seminole Hard Rock Hotel & Casino near Tampa, Fla. Those charges were later dropped. The Vikings expect Addison and all of the starting skill players to be present this spring to work with their newly configured quarterbacks room featuring Kyler Murray. This move, at the very least, secures Addison at a fixed cost for the 2027 season.
